 Advertisement Evacuation warnings issued for some coastal Santa Cruz County neighborhoods
 Santa Cruz County Sheriff's Office santa cruz county sheriff’s office evacuations SOURCE: Santa Cruz County Sheriff's Office Advertisement Updated: 3:23 PM PST Nov 13, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Josh Copitch Assistant News Director Evacuation warnings issued for some coastal Santa Cruz County neighborhoods
 Updated: 3:23 PM PST Nov 13, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Josh Copitch Assistant News Director CAPITOLA, Calif. — Evacuation warnings have been issued for four zones in Santa Cruz County as a winter storm is expected to bring waves of 25-35 feet to the Central Coast. 
 The warnings were issued at 2 p.m. on Friday by the Santa Cruz County Sheriff's Office and the Capitola Police Department. 
 Advertisement CTL-E048 - Las Olas Drive and Beach Drive areas
 CTL-E031 - Pot Belly Beach Rd area
 CTL-E027-A - Capitola wharf, south of cliff drive and west of Soquel Creek
 CTL-E029-B - Capitola Village, between Capitola Ave., and Monterey Ave. and areas west of Riverview Ave. and south of the railroad track. 
 >> Know your zone and see the live evacuation map. 
 According to meteorologist Erica Hoyte, one of the biggest concerns Friday and heading into the weekend will be along our coastline. An Alert Day has been issued for Saturday for the Monterey Peninsula and Santa Cruz due to dangerous surf conditions. A High Surf Warning begins this evening and continues through early Sunday morning.
 Breaking waves could reach 25 to 35 feet, with even larger waves possible at some exposed beaches. Dangerous sneaker waves and powerful rip currents will create life-threatening conditions for anyone near the water.
 Beaches, state parks closed as 35-foot waves are expected from first winter storm of the season This is a developing story, stay with KSBW 8 for the latest.
